title: Console hint palette: contextual templates for dashboards, rollouts, and cost views (Design Spec, 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This document specifies the v1 design for a lightweight, context-aware “hint palette” in the Redwood Console. The palette provides contextual templates and guided actions on dashboards, rollout pages, and cost views—especially when pages are empty or have low signal. The intent is to reduce time-to-first-success for new users while preserving guardrails and avoiding disruptive modals.
problem_statement: New users and low-activity teams frequently land on empty dashboards, rollout lists, and cost views with limited guidance on what to do next. Today’s empty states are readable but not actionable enough, and do not consistently connect users to recommended Console blueprints, runtime best practices, or cost-saving actions. This leads to slower activation (e.g., no dashboards created), misconfigured rollouts, and low engagement with cost optimization.
goals: 1) Reduce confusion in empty/low-data states. 2) Increase creation of dashboards and rollouts by new users. 3) Surface cost-saving recommendations in cost views. 4) Provide a low-friction path to templates and (optional) sample data without breaking platform guardrails.
non_goals: 1) Full in-product tour framework across the entire Console. 2) Personalized recommendations based on sensitive customer data. 3) Live, fully interactive template previews (explicitly deferred in v1).
scope_v1_pages: Dashboards landing + dashboard create flow entry points; Rollouts list + create rollout entry points; Cost view (overview + recommendations entry points).
user_experience_overview: The hint palette is a docked micro-panel that appears when a page is empty or low-signal. It presents a small set of contextual cards (Quick Actions, Starter Templates, and optional Walkthroughs). The user can apply a template with one click, open a prefilled configuration, or launch a short guided sequence. The palette can be dismissed and will stay dismissed for that page for the current user (with a global setting to re-enable).
information_hierarchy: Order of emphasis: (1) Quick Actions (1–2 items), (2) Starter Templates (2–4 items), (3) Walkthroughs (0–2 items). If a page is not empty but still low-signal, show only Quick Actions + a single “Browse templates” link (no walkthroughs).
placement_and_behavior: V1 placement is a docked panel on the right side of the content area (not in the page header). This was changed from the earlier header-docked concept to avoid header crowding with filters and to keep the palette aligned with primary content. The panel is non-modal and does not capture focus; it is reachable via keyboard navigation and can be collapsed. Dismissal is a single action: “Dismiss suggestions”. Re-enable is available via Settings > Help & Hints > “Show contextual suggestions”.
template_tiers_definition: Quick Actions: single-click creates or navigates (e.g., “Create dashboard from recommended template”). Starter Templates: opens a prefilled form with editable fields and a clear “Apply” CTA. Walkthroughs: short, step-by-step helper for first-time tasks (kept minimal in v1 and only on the emptiest states).
preview_strategy_v1: Static thumbnails are used for template cards in v1. Engineering feedback indicated live previews increase runtime and GPU cost and can degrade page performance. Thumbnails are generated at publish-time for template definitions and served via CDN; cards do not render charts or interactive widgets until applied.
content_rules_and_guardrails: Template content must not include customer data. Templates may include placeholder sample values, but any sample data import must be explicit and reversible. Cost recommendations must be phrased as suggestions and link to documentation; no automatic changes in v1. Rollout templates must respect org-level policies and permissions; if the user lacks permissions, show a disabled state with a short explanation and link to request access.
empty_state_triggers: Dashboards: show palette when user has 0 dashboards or current dashboard has 0 widgets. Rollouts: show palette when there are 0 rollouts OR when last rollout activity is older than 30 days (low-signal mode shows reduced set). Cost view: show palette when cost data is unavailable OR when no recommendations are present (show “Configure cost sources” quick action).
accessibility_requirements: The palette must be usable with keyboard and screen readers. Do not use focus traps in v1 walkthroughs; walkthrough steps should be linear and dismissible. Provide ARIA labels for all template cards and CTAs; ensure color contrast meets WCAG AA for hint badges and panel chrome. The collapse/expand control must be reachable and announce state changes.
analytics_and_measurement: Instrument the following events: hint_palette_shown, hint_palette_dismissed, hint_palette_collapsed, template_card_clicked, template_applied, template_apply_failed, walkthrough_started, walkthrough_step_completed, walkthrough_exited, settings_hints_toggled. Include properties: page_type (dashboard|rollout|cost), state (empty|low_signal|normal), template_id, template_tier, cohort_id (for experiment). Success metrics: time-to-first-dashboard (median), template application rate, rollout creation rate, and 7-day retention for new sign-ups.
experiment_plan: Run an A/B test on new sign-ups: 20% treatment / 80% control for 14 days. Guardrail metrics: page load time (P95), error rate for template apply, and support ticket volume tagged “onboarding/confusion”. Stop criteria: +5% or more increase in P95 load time on impacted pages, or statistically significant increase in apply_failed.
usability_testing_summary: Moderated usability testing was completed with 8 participants (mix of PLG sign-ups and internal developers) focusing on time-to-create-dashboard and comprehension of rollout templates. Key findings: users preferred a non-modal panel; they understood Quick Actions fastest; they asked for clearer permission messaging on rollout templates; and they wanted an obvious way to re-enable hints after dismissal. These findings directly informed the right-docked placement, the simplified dismissal model, and the Settings re-enable toggle.
implementation_notes_for_engineering: FE should implement the palette shell as a reusable component with page-level adapters that provide (a) trigger state, (b) recommended cards, and (c) permission gating. Card payloads should be backed by a template registry (IDs, titles, tier, thumbnail URL, destination, and required permissions). Thumbnails must be lazy-loaded. Ensure telemetry fires only once per page view for hint_palette_shown (debounce on rerenders).
open_questions: 1) Final policy for persistence of dismissal: per-page vs global (current v1: per-page per-user + global re-enable). 2) Whether cost recommendations should include links to auto-generated reports in v1 or remain documentation-only. 3) Localization scope: v1 English-only vs include top 3 locales.
changelog: 2026-02-20: Initial concept captured from product kick-off; targeted new sign-ups and low-activity teams; connect templates to Console blueprints and runtime recommendations. 2026-02-26: Engineering review flagged performance impact of live previews; agreed on static thumbnails for v1. 2026-03-05: Design iteration moved from modal concept to a docked panel and introduced a single dismiss action + global settings toggle. 2026-03-09: Accessibility review added requirements for no focus traps and improved ARIA coverage. 2026-03-14: Usability testing completed (8 participants); updated permission messaging and re-enable behavior. 2026-03-18: Placement updated to right-docked panel; analytics event names finalized; experiment plan updated to 20% treatment; release target moved to console-2026.05.
